content.summary_of_the_paper:
This paper mainly proposes an adaptive preconditioned gradient descent method, i.e., a PGD-MAML algorithm, which can adapt in a task-specific and path-dependent way. According to the experiment results, the method has its advantage in some tasks.

More specifically, MAML aims to train a model that can be fast adapted to different tasks by few shots and PGD-MAML adopts a preconditioned gradient descent in the inner-loop optimization. The existing work already made the preconditioner adaptive, task-specific, or iteration-dependent. The new method in this paper makes the preconditioner fully adaptive, i.e., both task-specific and iteration-dependent (which is called path-dependent in the paper due to the parameters containing more information).
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength
The major novel part of the paper is to make preconditioners in PGD-MAML fully adaptive. 
Besides, the method of parameterizing the scale matrix of SVD by multiplying diagonal matrices may inspire more related methods.
If its originality belongs to this paper (which is not quite sure yet to the reviewer), it will convince me more of the importance of the paper.
Experiments are relatively comprehensive. The results support the claims that the method achieves or in some cases outperforms the state of the art.

Weaknesses
The new method makes progress on the path of PGD-MAML. Certainly, the originality or novelty does not exceed PGD or adaptive PGD.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper is well written, and the references are complete enough to guide readers to find sources.
The major novelty is the new fully adaptive method.
Reproducibility is fine since the training details are given in the appendix. But, it would be much more helpful if the code can be open-sourced
content.summary_of_the_review:
The paper mainly makes progress on PGD-MAML by making the preconditioners fully adaptive. It also investigates its properties.
The endeavors to make the method more practical by introducing SVD approximation and comparing the number of parameters of different models are worthy.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new method called Geometry-Aware Meta-Learning (GAML) that aims to overcome the limitations MAML methods. In the initial analyses, GAML performs on par with the state-of-the-art MAML family and PGD-MAML family for a variety of few-shot learning tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The paper addresses reparameterizing weights in MAML methods for few-shot tasks. This problem has been recently studied in various related works.

Although this proposal is interesting, there are various major and minor problems with the paper. First, the claims and the proposed methods are not well justified. In several theoretical statements, there are overclaims. In addition, experimental analyses should be improved using additional datasets and models.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper proposes preconditioning parameters for MAML methods in few-shot learning tasks. This approach has been addressed in several recent works.

Conceptually, the paper claims that preconditioning matrix is a PSD matrix therefore is it is a Riemannian metric. Indeed, this claim is not correct in general since not all preconditioning, or matrix scaling matrices define Riemannian metrics. There are additional requirements to be satisfied such as  mapping on tangent spaces of the corresponding Riemannian manifolds. However, these requirements were not analyzed in the paper. 

Another claim is that the proposed preconditioning matrix defines the geometry of the loss surface since it is a Riemannian metric. Following the previous issue, this property is not utilized in the proposed Algorithm. That is, the proposed preconditioning matrix affects the geometry of the loss surface, but this is not due to its Riemannian structure. To sum up, it is not clear why the proposed method is called “Geometry-aware” since it does not make use of the geometry explicitly.

Another major issue with the paper is the experimental analyses. First, similar methods were studied in several previous works such as:
 
M. Hiller, M. Harandi, and T. Drummond, On Enforcing Better Conditioned Meta-Learning for Rapid Few-Shot Adaptation. Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), 2022.

X. Fan, Y. Wu, Z. Gao, Y. Jia, and M. Harandi (oral) Efficient Riemannian Meta-Optimization by Implicit Differentiation. AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence (AAAI), Virtual Conference, 2022.

The proposed methods should be compared with state-of-the-art in detail. For instance, there are some comparisons with Hiller given for conv4 models. Additional results should be given for ResNets and other models as well as for FC100 and Cifar-FS datasets. 

Moreover, please provide memory consumption and running time (training and inference) analyses in comparison with the state-of-the-art methods to explore how the proposed pre-conditioning increases complexity of models.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The paper addresses reparameterizing weights in MAML methods for few-shot tasks. This problem has been recently studied in various related works.

The proposed method perform on par with state-of-the-art. Therefore, additional analyses are required to justify its novelty and benefits more clearly. There are also several problems in the conceptual and theoretical statements. Therefore, the paper is not ready for publication.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper4029 by Reviewer FGjo

content.title: Response to reviewer FGjo
content.comment:
Thanks for your feedback. Let us provide a few corrections on the following misunderstandings.
 
1. Defining the Riemannian metric is equivalent to defining a mapping function into tangent spaces and Symmetric positive matrix (SPD) corresponds to Riemannian metric. In our manuscript, we skiped this explanation because we firmly believed it is trivial and does not need to be mentioned. In this regard, we will add detailed explanations on this relationship in our updated manuscript. 

2. The contributions of the two papers mentioned by the reviewer are different from ours. 

- [1] proposes a method for regularizing the Hessian condition number. They claim that this achieves the indirect effect of gradient preconditioning. On the contrary, we propose a preconditioner that satisfies full adaptation and the Riemannian metric. 

- [2] proposes an advanced method based on "Learning to learn by gradient descent by gradient descent" (NIPS 2016). They argue that it is efficient to use a Riemannian manifold as opposed to (NIPS2016) that is based on Euclidean space. On the other hand, we propose a MAML-based gradient preconditioning method.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a meta-learned preconditioner for adaptive to few-shot tasks using gradient-based methods. The proposed method is based on multiplying the spectrum of a reshaping of gradient matrices. It is analyzed theoretically and evaluated on standard few-shot synthetic and image classification tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
### Strengths:
1. The problem of designing a preconditioner that depends on every step in the training trajectory is interesting.
2. The method obtains strong performance on standard benchmarks in few-shot meta-learning.
3. The writing is fairly clear.

### Weaknesses:
1. The provided justification for the method is extremely limited. Via Theorem 1 the authors claim that the induced preconditioner is (1) a Riemannian metric and (2) depends on each step in the trajectory, but it is trivial to construct a preconditioner that satisfies these properties (just multiply the gradient by a small constant plus the absolute value of the parameter). Theorem 1 does not justify why the specific scheme outlined here is the right one to use. There is no discussion in the actual method derivation of why we should reshape the gradient in the specified way or why it is good to multiply the spectrum of the resulting matrix.
2. Theorem 2 justifying the approximation scheme is misleading, hiding an assumption in the appendix proof that the gradient is sampled from an i.i.d. normal distribution.
3. While the cost of SVD is heavily discussed, the additional cost incurred by full-trajectory dependence is not discussed.
4. Code is not provided.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: the writing is fairly clear, although Theorem 2 hides a strong assumption.  
Quality: the empirical results seem strong but the methodological justification is poor.  
Novelty: although preconditioning for meta-learning is heavily studied, having it depend on every step of the trajectory seems novel.  
Reproducibility: poor.
content.summary_of_the_review: I do not believe should be accepted in its current form due to the methodological issues and misleading statements outlined above.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

display_title: Official Review of Paper4029 by Reviewer 3wgN

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a novel variant of MAML for meta-learning and one-shot learning, which meta-learns a diagonal matrix that is used as a multiplicative factor over the singular values of the gradient matrix, corresponding to a specific preconditioner for SGD. Several proofs are given, including that the preconditioner induces a Riemannian metric and that the preconditioner is task-aware and adaptive. Several SOTA experimental results are presented.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The main strengths of the paper are that the method has a clear motivation, and the paper itself is written very clearly and to a high standard. The proposed method seems novel enough, and the experimental results are clearly superior.

The main negative aspect is a series of ommissions in the derivations and unstated assumptions, resulting in critical errors in the proofs, which if unresolved call into question the main theoretical claims that are repeated throughout the paper. They are:

Theorem 1:
"Since D is trivially symmetric positive definite" (Appendix B, page 14) is an incorrect assumption. D is similar (as in "similar matrices") to M, which is diagonal, so they should have the same number of positive eigenvalues. But there is no constraint on M's values to be strictly positive. I understand that in practice they are initialized to 1 and may hopefully not drift close to 0, but this is not guaranteed. The authors need to state this assumption up-front in the theorem formulation (so making it clear that it is required of the implementation), and justify why it is violated in the algorithm (or propose a way to respect it, e.g. with a softplus + epsilon reparameterization). Failure to do so means that the method does not induce a Riemannian metric, as claimed. The authors could also verify that the values of M never get close to 0 (or negative).

Theorem 1 is further violated in the "approximate" version of the proposed GAML: In addition to the same problem that M would need to be strictly positive, it no longer depends on the task-specific parameter theta, which is the other result of Theorem 1 -- making it no more adaptive than the baseline methods.

Theorem 2:
"Since independent vectors are located on the unit sphere, the vectors are asymptotically orthogonal as n increases by Lemma 1." (Appendix B, page 16) is a leap in logic that needs to be supported, because the assumptions of Lemma 1 and of Theorem 2 are different. The assumption in Theorem 2 is that the vectors are sampled from a normal distribution and re-normalized. The assumption in Lemma 1 is that they are uniformly-distributed over the sphere. It remains to be proved that they are equivalent -- merely stating that the vectors "are located" on the unit sphere does not mean that they are distributed in the same way.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
As mentioned in the strengths, the clarity and quality are very good. The novelty is moderate-to-high: it is not a large departure from previous methods in PGD-MAML, which experimented with different preconditioners, but the proposed one is indeed novel.

There are some issues with reproducibility:
1) Experimental and implementation details are somewhat sparse (what were the hyper-parameters? how were they chosen?), and no source code is available.
2) The results in Table 1 are "almost too good" -- in some configurations it represents a 10-fold improvement! This is great, but calls for greater scrutiny into the experimental setup, to rule out any inadvertent mistakes -- the source code would address this question.

Clarity could be improved by swapping sections 2.2 and 2.3, since the unfolding operation in section 2.2 is introduced without context (why do we need to reshape tensors into a matrix?), and having section 2.3 before would make it clear why it's needed.

A few more unclear aspects:

1. Why was mode-1 unfolding picked? A discussion of what is expected to happen if other modes are picked would be helpful.

2. In section 4.3, did the authors use the approximate version of GAML or the exact one? This should be specified.

3. How was the gap for figure 2 calculated exactly? (Could be in the appendix but needs to be reported.)
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall the paper has good ideas, is well presented, and has good results. Nevertheless, it cannot be published if it contains critical faults in the derivations and the line of reasoning is not laid out rigorously following from well-defined assumptions. I believe that the authors can correct this, but it remains the most important factor in a final decision (with reproducibility a close second factor). I will recommend rejection in the current state but will be happy to recommend acceptance if the authors address the above issues.
content.correctness: 1: The main claims of the paper are incorrect or not at all supported by theory or empirical results.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.title: We appreciate all the reviewers for the careful review and valuable feedback.
content.comment:
We appreciate all the reviewers for the careful review and valuable feedback. We are glad to hear that most of the reviewers acknowledge the work’s clarity in writing and novelty in the algorithm. 

However, as the reviewers have commented, we agree that our paper needs to provide more detailed and relevant explanation for the algorithm. Therefore, we have decided to withdraw our submission for ICLR 2023. After reflecting most of the feedback to our work and carefully revising our manuscript, we will re-submit our study to another venue. 

By the way, there are several points where the reviewers misunderstood, and we will make sure to clarify in the updated draft. Some of them are explained in the response to the reviewer FGjo.

Again, thank you very much for carefully reviewing our paper.
